geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the stepped body in a courtyard-capable macro so the next compile can create a ground-level public opening while preserving the dominant mass ancestry.
Introduce a courtyard void tied to the dominant mass to strengthen public threshold logic.
Size the courtyard as a meaningful public subtraction.
Open the court to the access side so it supports the neighborhood public edge contract.

graph_edits.rationale: Retain the dominant stepped body but change the macro to an envelope that can accept a targeted public carve without losing the clear mass hierarchy.
Add a meaningful public void to address the access edge and convert the sealed base into a legible neighborhood threshold.
Use a modest courtyard margin so the subtraction is substantial enough to read as public space rather than a decorative indentation.
Align the opening to the program-frame access side so the void becomes a true street-facing threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single coherent stepped mass with clear hierarchy and decent parcel discipline. It is not overly fragmented or collision-prone across views, and the stepped silhouette is legible as one continuous cascading body rather than arbitrary tiering. The main weakness is programmatic: for neighborhood living, the form currently behaves more like a compact object/terraced block than a building with a meaningful public threshold. The blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly; there is no obvious undercut, court, notch, or terrace opening that activates the street edge. Because the geometry still plausibly supports mixed-use neighborhood living and the mass remains internally consistent, it passes, but with a clear need to carve a public void or entry seam toward the access side in the next iteration.
